newsitem.title: ISRAEL: TAT Tech unveils "green" air conditioner.
newsitem.headline: TAT Tech unveils "green" air conditioner.

text.p: Israel's TAT Technologies Ltd expects to begin winning orders for its Environmentally Friendly Air Conditioning System (EFACS) after recently solving key technical problems, president Israel Ofen said on Thursday.

He said the underlying technology for EFACS, which does not employ gases that harm the environment, was perfected a year ago but only recently had the company resolved all the problems relating to the electronics of the system.
Ofen said TAT had already received an order for an demonstration unit from an unidentified European company. "If the demo model is okay, we're set," he said.

The earliest version of the EFACS was completed in 1992, and the company at the time won a big order from another European company, Ofen said. But problems with the system caused the company to cancel the order.
Ofen said TAT is pursuing the contract again. "We have a pretty good chance (of winning it). It would be a pretty big contract," he said.
Ofen refused to speculate about the scope of sales TAT could expect from EFACS this year.
The EFACS is designed for airplanes, buses and trains. Ofen said the company had not yet decided how it would approach the market for building air conditioners.
TAT Technologies is principally engaged in the manufacture, repair and overhaul of heat transfer equipment for aircraft, defence systems, electronic equipment and other applications.
The company had revenues of $4 million in the first nine months of 1996, leaving it with a $377,000 loss.
